panels: The allocation panel draws the held asset-class totals from the snapshot class totals through the existing ClassTotals, or the worded whole-remainder state; the Largest positions panel draws the ten largest securities by value from the snapshot security nodes, folded by identity, nulls last.
states: With no snapshot the panels say the holdings are loading, or that they could not be loaded when the read failed; with a snapshot they show the allocation or its worded remainder state, and always print the three not-published lines.
mount: ReportingTab renders PerformanceHoldingsPanels once, immediately before the DB-b-307 template comment, passing snapshot={header?.snapshot ?? null} and failed={header?.snapshotFailed ?? false}, outside the dashboardServed branch.
words: The Performance tab gains one component, PerformanceHoldingsPanels, and one mount in ReportingTab. The component draws the held allocation by asset class through the existing ClassTotals over classTotalsView (or the worded whole-remainder state), and the ten largest positions by value through securityRowsFrom and foldSecurityRows, nulls last. It shows the loading and failure sentences when there is no snapshot, and three always-shown absent lines: allocation over time, attribution and sector. No change or mover panel is built, because the snapshot carries no change field. The mount passes header snapshot and snapshotFailed and sits outside the dashboard branch. The mount test exercises the refusal branch of the tab only. Not proven here: no browser walk at Global, no DEV or PROD change, no read of what a real Cottonwood or Inflection snapshot holds, and no donut. The first act found the order's branch name held by a stale scratch worktree; a later read found it freed and the checkout succeeded; this is recorded as IRPT_DASHBD-D2-W249-S1.
